review_notes: Read the whole file and checked the Basis.linearMap_apply_apply statement in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/ToLin.lean, which the `split` in baseChange_linearMap uses. That use looks acceptable. The one finding is the proof of basis_repr_symm_apply, which unfolds the private construction. I did not compile the suggested replacement, so it may need small simp-lemma adjustments.

findings.problem: The proof unfolds both `basis` and `basisAux`. It then depends on simp normalising the `Equiv.uniqueProd` / `finsuppTensorFinsupp` / `TensorProduct.congr` / `Finsupp.lcongr` chain, using the explicit lemma `Equiv.uniqueProd_symm_apply`. The public lemma `basis_repr_tmul`, proved just above, already gives the forward behaviour of `(basis A b).repr`. Any routine change to how `basisAux` is assembled (for example a different equivalence for the `PUnit` factor or a reordered composition) would break this proof. It would also break if simp-normal forms of the symm of those equivalences changed.
findings.proposed_change: Prove it through the public interface, without unfolding `basis` or `basisAux`. Rewrite with `LinearEquiv.symm_apply_eq`, so the goal becomes `Finsupp.single i a = (basis A b).repr (a ⊗ₜ b.repr.symm (Finsupp.single i 1))`. Then use `basis_repr_tmul`, `Basis.repr_symm_single` (or `LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply`) and `Finsupp.mapRange_single`/`Finsupp.smul_single`, so the proof only needs `map_one` and `smul_eq_mul`. The proof then depends only on the stated characterisation of `basis_repr_tmul`.
findings.benefit: The proof no longer depends on the internal construction of `basisAux` or on `Equiv.uniqueProd_symm_apply`. The definition can be refactored without breaking it, and the argument (a basis vector maps to `single i 1`) is visible to the reader.

evidence.excerpt: (basis A b).repr (a ⊗ₜ m) = a • Finsupp.mapRange (algebraMap R A) (map_zero _) (b.repr m)
